events.summary: STORY: Samsung Electronics and its union didn't reach a pay deal on Wednesday, which risked a massive strike.The update followed long government-mediated talks on Monday and Tuesday.Any industrial action could impact the wider South Korean economy.The country's authorities were so concerned they called an emergency meeting.Prime Minister Kim Min-seok told the government to closely manage the situation and encourage more dialogue to prevent a strike.Samsung shares fell as much as 6% after the news broke, but later traded up 1% after the update of the ministerial meeting.Rival SK Hynix saw its stock surge 7%.It was helped by market views it could profit from Samsung's labor issues, and expectations it will list in the U.S later this year.Samsung's union is angry over what it calls a massive gap in bonus pay with SK Hynix.It has planned an 18-day strike from May 21 if its demand aren't met.The union has warned more than 50,000 workers could walk off the job.That would likely delay shipments to customers and further push up chip prices.The union has called for an end to a cap on bonus pay currently set at 50% of annual base salary.It also wants the allocation of 15% of annual operating profit to bonus pay and more clarity on how bonuses are calculated.The union said it has no plans to resume talks before the strike date.But added it would consider "a proper proposal" if the company presents one.Samsung said it regretted the collapse of talks and will continue to have "sincere dialogue" with the union to stop what it called a worst-case scenario.
events.title: Samsung Electronics fails to reach union deal; PM wants strike averted
